the nonlinear wavelet estimators of the hazard rate function are consistent, have the same rate of convergence and the same asymptotic mean integrated squared error as the kernel estimators, and have the same asymptotic normality.
the wavelet estimator of a hazard rate based on censored and uncensored data is asymptotically unbiased and has the minimum mean integrated squared error.
the nonlinear wavelet-based estimator of hazard rate function is consistent, asymptotically normal, and has a MISE that converges to zero at the optimal rate.

the development of new methods for estimating the hazard rate function based upon censored data.
the development of new statistical methods and theory for analyzing censored data by wavelets.
the development of wavelet-based hazard estimation methods for censored data.

the wavelet estimator is asymptotically normal, has the same asymptotic expansion for the MISE as kernel estimators, and is more robust to the irregularity of the underlying hazard function.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, under randomly censored survival data, the wavelet estimator has the same asymptotic expansion and asymptotic normality as the corresponding kernel estimator, but the rate of the convergence of the wavelet estimator is faster than the kernel estimator.
wavelets are better than kernels in estimating hazard rates based on censored samples, especially when the hazard rates have discontinuities and the sample sizes are large.

, the asymptotic properties of nonlinear wavelet estimators are similar to that of kernel estimators, but the nonlinear wavelet estimations can achieve better accuracy in terms of the MISE than the kernel estimators, when the underlying function is not smooth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wavelets provide a powerful tool for estimating a hazard rate function from censored data when the underlying hazard function is only piecewise smooth.
the MISE for the nonlinear wavelet hazard rate estimator is of order O(n-2/3), while the analogous MISE for the kernel hazard rate estimator is at least O(n-1/2).
wavelet methods are a powerful tool for the analysis of censored data.
